    29	Below we will provide samples on how to send cloudevents using the popular
    30	[`requests`](http://docs.python-requests.org) library.
    31	
    32	### Binary HTTP CloudEvent
    33	
    34	```python
    35	from cloudevents.http import CloudEvent, to_binary
    36	import requests
    37	
    38	# Create a CloudEvent
    39	# - The CloudEvent "id" is generated if omitted. "specversion" defaults to "1.0".
    40	attributes = {
    41	    "type": "com.example.sampletype1",
    42	    "source": "https://example.com/event-producer",
    43	}
    44	data = {"message": "Hello World!"}
    45	event = CloudEvent(attributes, data)
    46	
    47	# Creates the HTTP request representation of the CloudEvent in binary content mode
    48	headers, body = to_binary(event)
    49	
    50	# POST
    51	requests.post("<some-url>", data=body, headers=headers)
    52	```
    53	
    54	### Structured HTTP CloudEvent
    55	
    56	```python
    57	from cloudevents.http import CloudEvent, to_structured
    58	import requests
    59	
    60	# Create a CloudEvent
    61	# - The CloudEvent "id" is generated if omitted. "specversion" defaults to "1.0".
    62	attributes = {
    63	    "type": "com.example.sampletype2",
    64	    "source": "https://example.com/event-producer",
    65	}
    66	data = {"message": "Hello World!"}
    67	event = CloudEvent(attributes, data)
    68	
    69	# Creates the HTTP request representation of the CloudEvent in structured content mode
    70	headers, body = to_structured(event)
    71	
    72	# POST
    73	requests.post("<some-url>", data=body, headers=headers)
    74	```

    77	
    78	## Receiving CloudEvents
    79	
    80	The code below shows how to consume a cloudevent using the popular python web framework
    81	[flask](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/1.1.x/quickstart/):
    82	
    83	```python
    84	from flask import Flask, request
    85	
    86	from cloudevents.http import from_http
    87	
    88	app = Flask(__name__)
    89	
    90	
    91	# create an endpoint at http://localhost:/3000/
    92	@app.route("/", methods=["POST"])
    93	def home():
    94	    # create a CloudEvent
    95	    event = from_http(request.headers, request.get_data())
    96	
    97	    # you can access cloudevent fields as seen below
    98	    print(
    99	        f"Found {event['id']} from {event['source']} with type "
   100	        f"{event['type']} and specversion {event['specversion']}"
   101	    )
   102	
   103	    return "", 204
   104	
   105	
   106	if __name__ == "__main__":
   107	    app.run(port=3000)

from cloudevents.http import CloudEvent

def test_comprehensive_equality():
    """Test CloudEvent equality comprehensively"""

    attributes1 = {
        "source": "test-source-1",
        "type": "test.type.one",
        "specversion": "1.0"
    }
    
    attributes2 = {
        "source": "test-source-2", 
        "type": "test.type.two",
        "specversion": "1.0"
    }
    
    data1 = {"key": "value1"}
    data2 = {"key": "value2"}
    
    event1 = CloudEvent(attributes1, data1)
    event2 = CloudEvent(attributes1, data1)  # Same as event1
    event3 = CloudEvent(attributes1, data2)  # Different data
    event4 = CloudEvent(attributes2, data1)  # Different attributes
    
    print("1. Testing CloudEvent to CloudEvent equality (should work as before):")
    print(f"   event1 == event2 (same attrs+data): {event1 == event2} (expected: True)")
    print(f"   event1 == event3 (same attrs, diff data): {event1 == event3} (expected: False)")
    print(f"   event1 == event4 (diff attrs, same data): {event1 == event4} (expected: False)")
    print(f"   event1 != event3: {event1 != event3} (expected: True)")
    
    assert event1 == event2, "Equal events should be equal"
    assert not (event1 == event3), "Events with different data should not be equal"
    assert not (event1 == event4), "Events with different attributes should not be equal"
    assert event1 != event3, "Not equals should work"
    
    print("   ✓ CloudEvent to CloudEvent comparisons work correctly\n")
    
    print("2. Testing CloudEvent to non-CloudEvent equality (the fix):")
    test_cases = [
        (1, "integer"),
        ("string", "string"),
        (None, "None"),
        ([], "empty list"),
        ({}, "empty dict"),
        (3.14, "float"),
        (True, "boolean"),
        (object(), "generic object"),
    ]
    
    all_passed = True
    for value, description in test_cases:
        try:
            result_eq = event1 == value
            result_ne = event1 != value
            print(f"   event1 == {description}: {result_eq} (expected: False)")
            print(f"   event1 != {description}: {result_ne} (expected: True)")
            
            if result_eq != False:
                print(f"   ✗ FAIL: Expected False, got {result_eq}")
                all_passed = False
            if result_ne != True:
                print(f"   ✗ FAIL: Expected True, got {result_ne}")
                all_passed = False
                
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"   ✗ ERROR with {description}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            all_passed = False
    
    if all_passed:
        print("   ✓ All non-CloudEvent comparisons work correctly\n")
    else:
        print("   ✗ Some non-CloudEvent comparisons failed\n")
        return False
    
    print("3. Testing edge cases:")

    class CloudEventSubclass(CloudEvent):
        pass
    
    subclass_event = CloudEventSubclass(attributes1, data1)
    try:
        result = event1 == subclass_event
        print(f"   event1 == subclass_event: {result}")
        # This should work since subclass is instance of CloudEvent
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"   ✗ ERROR with subclass: {e}")
        all_passed = False
    
    # Test symmetric property
    try:
        result1 = event1 == 1
        result2 = 1 == event1
        print(f"   event1 == 1: {result1}")
        print(f"   1 == event1: {result2}")
        # Both should be False, but Python might handle the reverse differently
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"   ✗ ERROR with symmetric test: {e}")
        all_passed = False
        
    print("\n=== Test Summary ===")
    if all_passed:
        print("✓ ALL TESTS PASSED")
        return True
    else:
        print("✗ SOME TESTS FAILED")  
        return False

if __name__ == "__main__":

    exit(0 if success else 1)

from stix2 import TLPMarking

def test_exact_issue_scenario():

    # Create an AttackPattern similar to the CAPEC example from the issue
    ap = AttackPattern(
        name="Test Attack Pattern",
        description="A test pattern",
        allow_custom=True,
        x_capec_abstraction="Meta",
        x_capec_consequences=["Loss of Confidentiality"],
        x_capec_example_instances=["Example 1", "Example 2"],
        x_capec_likelihood_of_attack="High",
        x_capec_prerequisites=["Prerequisite 1"],
        x_capec_skills_required=["Low"],
        x_capec_typical_severity="Medium",
        x_resources_required=["Computer", "Internet"]
    )
    
    # Create a marking definition (similar to the issue)
    marking_def = MarkingDefinition(
        definition_type="tlp",
        definition=TLPMarking(tlp="green")
    )
    
    # This is the exact line that was failing in the issue:
    # ap.add_markings(marking_def_id)
    # where marking_def_id is marking_def.id
    
    print("Before adding markings:")
    print(f"Object has x_capec_abstraction: {hasattr(ap, 'x_capec_abstraction')}")
    print(f"x_capec_abstraction value: {ap.x_capec_abstraction}")
    
    try:
        # This should now work without throwing ExtraPropertiesError
        ap_with_markings = ap.add_markings(marking_def.id)
        
        print("\n✅ SUCCESS: add_markings worked without ExtraPropertiesError!")
        print(f"After adding markings:")
        print(f"Object has x_capec_abstraction: {hasattr(ap_with_markings, 'x_capec_abstraction')}")

        print(f"Marking refs: {ap_with_markings.get('object_marking_refs', [])}")
        
        # Verify all custom properties are preserved
        custom_props = [
            'x_capec_abstraction',
            'x_capec_consequences', 
            'x_capec_example_instances',
            'x_capec_likelihood_of_attack',
            'x_capec_prerequisites',
            'x_capec_skills_required',

        for prop in custom_props:
            assert hasattr(ap_with_markings, prop), f"Missing custom property: {prop}"
            
        print(f"\n✅ All {len(custom_props)} custom properties preserved!")
        
        return True
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n❌ FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

        traceback.print_exc()

if __name__ == "__main__":
